title: Dubai discounts: Apps, cards, and offers to save money in 2026
summary: Let’s look at apps, membership cards, bank cards, and everyday offers to help you save money in Dubai, from Ziina Violet to The Entertainer or Fazaa.
body_markdown:
Maybe it’s time for a new laptop, or you’re thinking about joining that gym you keep hearing about. Or maybe you just want to take a friend out to brunch.


Then you check the prices and start wondering: is there a way to get what you want for less?


Your bank credit card might come with dining deals you’ve never checked. Special offers from an app could cut the cost of your next day out. And if you’re planning a bigger purchase, waiting for one of the city’s major shopping events could make a huge difference.


Some Dubai discounts, including one-time vouchers and seasonal promotions, don’t require a membership. Other perks, like monthly benefits, points, and cashback, come through paid memberships, free loyalty programs, or cards with specific eligibility requirements.


The tricky part is knowing where to look for deals that are actually relevant to you.


This guide is here to help. By the end, you’ll know which deals you can use right away, which memberships could wind up paying for themselves, and which offers are worth planning around based on where you already spend.


Here are five ways to get started:


- Check the everyday perks that payment apps or cards like Ziina Violet can offer


- Use a discount app to find deals in Dubai


- See if you qualify for a Dubai discount card


- Join loyalty programs where you already spend


- Plan bigger purchases around Dubai’s seasonal sales


Ziina Violet helps you save on coffee, food delivery, rides, fitness, shopping, and more. Get up to AED 850+ in potential monthly value from 12 partner brands, plus zero Ziina currency fees on up to AED 20,000 in non-AED spending each month.

### Check if your bank debit or credit card comes with any benefits


Some UAE debit and credit cards come with their own dining, entertainment, or cashback programs.


For example, some eligible Emirates NBD and Liv cards give you access to Bon Appétit offers at participating restaurants. The available discounts and qualifying conditions vary by venue.


1


Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank (ADCB) also offers cards with lifestyle benefits. Their 365 Cashback Credit Card advertises 6% cashback on eligible local dining purchases, 3% on groceries, and 5% on fuel and Salik.


However, you’d typically need to spend at least AED 5,000 in a calendar month to qualify for cashback, and an annual fee applies after the first year.


2


But don’t skip over the fine print: A card might advertise generous cashback but require a minimum monthly spend. A restaurant discount could only apply at participating locations or on certain days.


Details like the membership fee, spending threshold, and redemption process will give you a sense of how often you could use the benefit and whether the savings are worth the cost.


One last thing: Two cards from the same bank can have very different perks, so make sure to check the conditions for each carefully.


## 2. Use a discount app to find great deals in Dubai


Already have a plan in mind and want to see if there’s a cheaper way to book it? A discount app might be your best bet. You could find a two-for-one offer for a family theme park visit or a spa experience priced below the usual rate.


These apps work in a couple of different ways.


Some charge a membership fee that gives you access to offers throughout the year. If you use them often enough, the discounts can add up to more than the membership costs.


Others sell individual vouchers: you pay a discounted price for a specific meal or experience, then use the voucher when you visit.


Before paying, check how far in advance you need to book, when the offer expires, and what happens if your plans change.


Here are a few options to explore:


### The ENTERTAINER


The ENTERTAINER is geared toward people who expect to regularly go out, book experiences, and redeem discount offers whenever they can throughout the year. Their signature Buy One Get One Free offers cover dining, attractions, fitness, beauty, and other lifestyle categories.


The ENTERTAINER UAE 2026 membership is listed at AED 395 including VAT and expires on December 30, 2026. It’s a fixed-term purchase, so buying later in the year gives you less time to use the offers.


3


Browse the participating venues before joining, though – the membership will feel a lot more valuable if the places you already like or genuinely want to try are included.


### Cobone


One-off discounts can make more sense when you’re looking to pay less for a specific activity, outing, or plan. Cobone could be a good option if that sounds like you.


They sell individual vouchers for restaurants, attractions, spa treatments, staycations, and other experiences. Choose an offer, pay online, and you’ll receive a voucher by email with instructions for using it – including any reservation requirements.


4


### Groupon


Groupon’s Dubai page currently lists more than 1,000 offers covering food, beauty, wellness, attractions, auto shops, and more.


You can find deals on popular attractions like a VIP Desert Safari adventure, quad bike rides, hotel packages with pool access – or even an affordable massage at Versailles Spa or Spa Suasana.


Some offers also include choices for different group sizes, like dinner for two or bowling with friends.


5


## 3. See if you qualify for a UAE discount card


Some of Dubai’s most comprehensive discount programs depend on where you work, your employer’s participation, or whether you’re a student.


That can make them easy to overlook – you could already qualify through work or school and have no idea the benefits are available to you.


Depending on the program, you might need to get a membership card, activate a benefit on an app, or use a discount code.


### Fazaa


Fazaa offers member discounts across shopping, dining, entertainment, travel, car maintenance, healthcare, and other everyday categories.


6


Membership is available to eligible groups, including employees of the Ministry of Interior and participating government or semi-government organizations. Registration is limited to specific companies, so you’ll need a company code from your employer to sign up.


7


This could be one of those workplace benefits that’s easy to miss in an onboarding email or employee portal. If your organization participates, it’s worth seeing what’s available before paying full price for your next meal, hotel stay, or car service.


### Esaad


Esaad is a discount membership program with a physical card, digital card, and mobile app. Some government employees qualify through their workplace, and the program also includes eligible retirees in Dubai.


Their app includes discounts on dining, hotel stays, education, healthcare, shopping, and more, covering both everyday spending and bigger expenses.


Eligible members can activate their account using UAE Pass or their Emirates ID. When it’s time to claim an offer, the app will either provide a discount code or let the merchant complete the redemption in person.


That range of offers means you could keep using the same membership for everyday plans and bigger expenses throughout the year. Check your eligibility directly with Esaad before planning around their deals.


### The nol ISIC card


Students also have a dedicated discount card option available through Dubai’s nol International Student Identity Card (ISIC). Students aged 5-23 who are enrolled at a school, college, or university in the UAE can apply through the nol Pay app.


The card costs AED 95 and comes with a 50% discount on RTA public transport fares, plus student offers covering travel, shopping, education, and entertainment in more than 130 countries.


9


## 4. Join loyalty programs where you already spend


Loyalty points might not seem super exciting after one purchase. But they get a lot more interesting once your usual grocery runs, dinners, movie outings, or hotel stays start building toward something you can actually redeem.


The key is to choose programs that give you points for purchasing from the places you already visit.


Just make sure you also understand what you have to do to earn points, whether that’s scanning a receipt, showing a membership number, or linking a payment card.


### SHARE Rewards


If you regularly visit Mall of the Emirates or a City Centre mall, there’s a good chance some of your usual spending could earn SHARE points.


SHARE lets members scan eligible shopping and dining receipts through the app at 17 malls across the UAE. You can redeem the points for a mall gift card and put it toward future shopping or dining.


10


That gives all those receipts you usually stuff into a bag or throw away a little more purpose. Open the SHARE app before getting rid of them and see if the purchase qualifies.


### U By Emaar


U By Emaar lets you earn points at participating hotels, restaurants, spas, places to visit, and selected malls.


The program is free to join – and a hotel stay, restaurant meal, spa visit, or trip to a local attraction can all contribute Upoints at eligible locations. The earning rate depends on where you spend. 10 Upoints are worth AED 1 when redeemed at participating venues.


11


### Skywards Everyday


Did you know that everyday purchases can also contribute toward your next travel reward?


Skywards Everyday lets Emirates Skywards members link up to five eligible Visa or Mastercard payment cards. Once the cards are connected, eligible purchases at participating brands earn Miles automatically.


12


Most partners award one Skywards Mile for every AED 3 spent, while grocery and pharmacy partners award one Mile for every AED 5.


## 5. Plan bigger purchases around Dubai’s seasonal sales


Sometimes, the easiest way to get a better price is to wait.


If you have a bigger purchase in mind and don’t need it right away, it could be worth holding off until one of Dubai’s seasonal sales.


Seasonal sales create plenty of urgency, so decide what you want before the discounts begin. Save the current price, set your budget, and make a note of the exact model or item so you’ll have a reference point when the offers start rolling in.


### Dubai Shopping Festival


Dubai Shopping Festival turns the winter shopping season into a citywide event, with retail offers, raffles, entertainment, concerts, and fireworks.


13


This is one of the bigger opportunities to plan around if you’ve been putting off any purchases. Watch for offers from the brands you like and time your shopping for a period like this, when brands are using discounts and offers to compete for your attention.


### Dubai Summer Surprises


Dubai Summer Surprises brings shopping offers, limited-time deals, and family entertainment during the summer months.


14 The timing could work well for summer clothing, family activities, staycations, or early back-to-school shopping.


Since the festival runs for a few weeks, you have more time to compare offers instead of feeling pressured to make every decision in one weekend.


### 3 Day Super Sale


The 3 Day Super Sale compresses citywide promotions into a much shorter window.


In the past, that’s included advertised discounts of up to 90% across fashion, beauty, lifestyle products, and other retail categories.


15


That short window can feel intense, so you might want to start your wishlist before participating retailers announce their offers.


### Black Friday, White Friday, and Yellow Friday


Black Friday is also part of the shopping calendar in the region, although you’ll see different names depending on the retailer. Amazon UAE runs White Friday promotions around late November, while noon uses the name Yellow Friday.


1617


This is another period to watch if you’re saving for electronics, replacing an appliance, or buying gifts.


Just keep in mind that retailers set their own sale dates, so offers can run over several days.


## Final thoughts on Dubai discounts and Ziina Violet


By now, you’ve seen how many different ways there are to save in Dubai. You’ll get the most value from offers that fit how you already spend, because those are the ones you’re most likely to remember and use.


If Violet’s partner categories fit your routine, you can get more from the brands and experiences you already enjoy. That could mean free coffee before work, credits toward your next fitness class, money back on shopping, or fewer fees on your next trip abroad.
